summary: Adds a suite-wide deployment-mode answer and Phase 1 multi-instance safety. A new shared model (`domain/shared/services/deployment.go`) tiers the five apps into genuinely clusterable (`myseliasan`, `myidsan` -- stateless over Postgres) versus single-instance by design (`mymatasan` owns capture pipelines/local recordings/GPU; `myiotsan` and `mypintusan` each hold a serial port open for the process's lifetime), and exposes a per-app `GET /api/deployment/preflight` readiness checklist (db engine, cache/lock reachability -- pinged, not just name-checked -- the at-rest encryption key's fingerprint for comparing across instances, JWT-secret provenance, per-instance DB pool budget) plus, on the two Tier-A apps, `GET`/`POST /api/deployment/mode` to declare `standalone`/`clustered`. A declared mode turns the existing boot-time shared-state warning from an inference into a stated fact. New `Cipher.Fingerprint()`/`KeyStore.Fingerprint()` (`infra/atrest`) give the at-rest key a comparable, non-secret identity distinct from the per-key-file install marker. Phase 1 also adds real multi-instance safety: `infra/coordination` gains `Locker.TryLock`/`Lock.Valid` and a leader-election primitive (`Elect`/`Leader.IsLeader`) built on them, wired into every app as `apphost.Dependencies.Leader`; myseliasan's notification rollup, retention purges, correlator sweep, dedup-ledger prune, heartbeat reconciliation, and AI digest schedule/purge are now leader-gated so a replicated deployment runs each exactly once instead of once per instance, and myidsan's audit-retention purge is gated the same way (its session gauge is deliberately left ungated, since it only reads and publishes a number to its own Prometheus scrape target). Schema bootstrap is separately serialized across instances starting together via a new deployment-wide migration lock. `transaction.lockProvider` is now editable beside the cache in both Tier-A apps' Settings `storage` section and in myidsan's setup wizard's "Where sessions live" step, so an operator can no longer reach a half-clustered install with a shared cache and a per-process lock. myseliasan's setup wizard gains a new Deployment step (before sign-in and node adoption); both Tier-A apps' Settings panels and the three Tier-B apps' Settings surfaces render the shared readiness checklist (read-only, with a fixed reason, for Tier B).
compatibility: Standalone behaviour is completely unchanged: with the default per-process (memory) lock provider, the single instance always wins leader election immediately and takes no migration lock, so every `leaderOnly`/`leaderTicker`/`RollupMaintainer.WithGate` guard added by this change is a no-op and every existing single-instance install behaves exactly as before. Declaring a deployment mode is optional and defaults to undeclared/standalone for every existing install; the boot-time warning falls back to its previous inference-only behaviour until an operator explicitly declares a mode. Two known gaps are NOT closed by this change and must not be read as 'myseliasan is now fully clusterable': (1) heartbeat/liveness reconciliation only sees nodes whose control channels are connected to the leader instance, so a healthy node attached to a different instance can eventually be marked lost and alert incorrectly (needs a shared node-owner registry, planned Phase 2); (2) fleet rules whose clauses span nodes attached to different instances never arm at all -- they go quiet rather than double-fire (needs a shared event bus, planned Phase 3). Also unchanged by this phase: the live notification feed (SSE) and the node proxy both remain per-instance, and the Settings editor still writes and restarts only the instance being talked to.
